newsitem.title: BELGIUM: MEPs seek better EU response to refugee crises.
newsitem.headline: MEPs seek better EU response to refugee crises.

text.p: As a new refugee crisis erupted on the Zaire-Rwanda border, the European Parliament is expected to call on November 13 for a swift and effective European Union reaction to such emergencies.
But the EU must on no account collaborate with attempts to make refugees return home by force, the parliament will say.

"Governments are increasingly more worried about not having refugees and asylum seekers on their doorstep than about respecting the principle of not forcing people to return when they are in fear of their lives," the author of a parliamentary report on EU aid to refugees in Asia and Latin America told Reuters.
The report, by British Socialist Richard Howitt, recommends a string of changes to the Council's common position on a draft regulation on aid to refugees -- COM(95)297.
"This is the EU's first legislation on refugees. We have to have the principle of non-refoulement in it. We cannot breach the (1951) Geneva Convention," Howitt said.
The MEP said he thought the member states were wary of setting a precedent.
"For example, it is clearly in the interest of the British government to get rid of the 'problem' of the Vietnamese boat people before the hand over of Hong Kong to China," he said.
Howitt, whose report won cross-party support from the parliament's development committee on Wednesday, said he expected the full assembly to back his call for a swift EU reaction to refugee crises.
This means simplifying the cumbersome bureaucratic structure for approving refugee aid projects worth over two million Ecus which Council wants to set up.
"(Aid) is time-sensitive. We are talking about refugees on the move," Howitt stressed.
But under the approval procedure sought by ministers, the European Commission would have to get permission in the 11 official EU languages before it could release the aid, he said.
"That means one in four projects will be delayed by three months," he explained.
"The deaths (last year) in Nepal refugee camps would be reproduced throughout Asia and Latin America whilst Luxembourg officials translated the necessary documents," his report says.

Among the other amendments to the proposal which parliament is expected to request is a call for the EU to target its aid Howitt's report says priority should be given to projects specifically designed to help women and children, who make up 80 percent of the population in refugee camps, and social groups which have been singled out for persecution.
